entries.label: Bad seeds
entries.summary: Leadership vacuums let long-term geopolitical dangers grow.
entries.quote: The geopolitical dangers taking shape around the world will bear fruit in years to come.

entries.label: US-China
entries.summary: The US-China relationship is broken beyond the trade dispute.
entries.quote: Something fundamental has broken in the relationship between Washington and Beijing that can't be put back together, regardless of what happens to their economic ties.

entries.label: Cyber gloves off
entries.summary: Cyber conflict grows while rules for it remain absent.
entries.quote: Hackers have grown more sophisticated, societies have become heavily dependent on digital services, and efforts to agree on basic rules of the road for cyber conflict have gone nowhere.

entries.label: European populism
entries.summary: Populists and protest movements are stronger than ever in Europe.
entries.quote: 2019 will show that populists and protest movements are stronger than ever.

entries.label: The US at home
entries.summary: US political volatility is very high though removal of Trump is unlikely.
entries.quote: While the odds of Trump being impeached and removed from office remain extremely low, political volatility will be exceptionally high.

entries.label: Innovation winter
entries.summary: Politics reduces capital and talent for emerging technologies.
entries.quote: We're heading for a global innovation winter—a politically driven reduction in the financial and human capital available to drive the next generation of emerging technologies.

entries.label: Coalition of the unwilling
entries.summary: More leaders refuse to uphold the liberal international order.
entries.quote: The US-led global order has been eroding for a couple of decades now, but we are now seeing the growing ranks of a coalition of world leaders unwilling to uphold the global liberal order, with some even bent on bringing it down.

entries.label: Mexico
entries.summary: AMLO's concentrated power brings domestic risk in Mexico.
entries.quote: The country's new president, Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, begins his term with a degree of power and control over the political system not seen in Mexico since the early 1990s, and domestic risk factors loom large.

entries.label: Ukraine
entries.summary: Russia-Ukraine tensions rise after the Kerch Strait clash.
entries.quote: November's clash in the Kerch Strait was a taste of coming tensions. Putin continues to see Ukraine as vital to Russia's sphere of influence.

entries.label: Nigeria
entries.summary: Nigeria's election is its most contested since 1999.
entries.quote: Nigeria faces its most fiercely contested election since the transition to democracy in 1999.

entries.label: Brexit
entries.summary: Eurasia Group marks Brexit with an asterisk because almost any outcome is still possible.
entries.quote: Why the asterisk? Because three years after the vote, almost any Brexit outcome remains possible.
entries.note: Printed as '*Brexit' after risk 10; not ranked.

entries.label: A return to dictatorship in Brazil
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects Brazil's institutions to prevent dangerous centralisation under Bolsonaro.
entries.quote: Brazil's new president Jair Bolsonaro might be a nationalist, but the country's institutions won't allow for any dangerous centralization of power.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Saudi Arabia
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects no serious risk to the Saudi crown prince or kingdom in 2019.
entries.quote: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has made many enemies, but neither he nor the kingdom face serious risks in 2019.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Iran
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects Iran's need for European ties to limit its aggression.
entries.quote: Iran's need to endure US sanctions by protecting relations with Europe will limit its aggressiveness.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Russia-China relations
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects suspicion to limit Russia-China cooperation.
entries.quote: Suspicion and competition will restrain Russia and China's cooperation.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

notes: The report adds an unranked asterisk item, 'Brexit', after risk 10, captured here as ranking 'wildcard'. Red herring labels are from the PDF; quotes from the landing-page summary.
